title: III–V. Modes of governing humans: instinct, institution, and teaching
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 1 John 4:1). take nothing away, or teach nothing contrary (1 Thessalonians 5:21; — if they add nothing to ye principles. Those mediately called stand as to be obeyed with this proviso: Mediately, when through parents, teachers, ministers belonging toward ye word, magistrates, plus other humans to whom He commits His word. Immediately, when by means belonging toward Himself, by means belonging toward ye Son plus Holy Spirit, by means belonging toward angels, by means belonging toward revealed word, by means belonging toward ye law belonging toward nature impressed, by means belonging toward conscience, by means belonging toward dreams plus visions, by means belonging toward miracles plus wonders, by means belonging toward special inspiration. Thus in a more notable respect God teaches humans both immediately plus mediately. V. By way belonging toward institution God governs human beings by means belonging toward teaching. IV. Second, governance stands as one thing by means belonging toward way belonging toward instinct, another by means belonging toward way belonging toward institution, another by means belonging toward way belonging toward fulfillment. III.
pass_b_english: III. Second, governance is one thing by way of instinct, another by way of institution, another by way of fulfillment. IV. By way of institution God governs human beings by teaching. V. Thus in a more notable respect God teaches humans both immediately and mediately. Immediately, when by Himself, by the Son and Holy Spirit, by angels, by revealed word, by the law of nature impressed, by conscience, by dreams and visions, by miracles and wonders, by special inspiration. Mediately, when through parents, teachers, ministers of the word, magistrates, and other humans to whom He commits His word. Those mediately called are to be obeyed with this proviso: if they add nothing to the principles, take nothing away, or teach nothing contrary (1 Thessalonians 5:21; 1 John 4:1).
source_text: III. Secundo alia est per modum instinctus, alia per modum institutionis, alia per modum impletionis. IV. Per modum institutionis Deus homines gubernat docendo. V. Sic insigniore respectu tum immediate tum mediate Deus homines docet. Immediate, cum per se ipsum, per Filium et Spiritum Sanctum, per angelos, per verbum revelatum, per legem naturae impressam, per conscientiam, per somnia et visiones, per miracula et prodigia, per inspirationem specialem. Mediate, cum per parentes, magistros, ministros verbi, magistratus, et alios homines, quibus verbum suum commendat. Mediate vocatis cum hac adiunctione est obtemperandum, si nihil principiis addant, demant aut contrarium doceant (1 Thess. 5:21; 1 Ioh. 4:1).
